svg.title: A request receipt, overdue work and a supplied contact record are separate facts
svg.desc: Four fictional clock readings are separate. At minute zero the request is accepted and its one-hour clock starts once; a retry keeps that time. At minute sixty, a supplied first-contact time can still meet the local rule. At sixty minutes plus one second, a local checker records overdue work but does not alert or contact anyone. A supplied first-contact time at hour four stays late. The fixture does not verify that a person reached the customer or that an AWS deadline service ran.

g.text: A receipt does not make the contact promise
Four different facts in one fictional repair request.
The clock starts once; a retry keeps the original time.
A supplied contact time here meets the fixture rule.
The local checker opens work; it makes no call.
The fixture marks it late; real contact is unverified.
An open worklist is not an alert, assigned owner or customer message.
Local design only; no AWS service or observed human delivery.
